description: DEF CON 31 Policy Village convenes government leaders, legislative advocates, and security researchers to debate cyber diplomacy, software liability, encryption rights, coordinated vulnerability disclosure, and youth cybercrime diversion.

talks.title: US Cyber Policy 101
talks.teaser: Harley Geiger and US government representatives provide a foundational briefing on federal cyber policy priorities, agency roles, and public engagement paths.
talks.summary:
Foundations of United States Cyber Policy

Navigating federal cybersecurity policy requires understanding the distinct roles, authorities, and jurisdictions of executive agencies, legislative bodies, and independent regulators.

Key Focus Areas and Strategic Directives

Policy leader Harley Geiger reviews major initiatives advancing through the executive branch and Congress, analyzing the rollout of the National Cybersecurity Strategy.

Agency Roles and Cross-Government Collaboration

Officials from key federal cyber agencies detail their respective missions, explaining how interagency partnerships coordinate defense, regulation, and incident response.

Mechanisms for Hacker Community Engagement

The panel outlines concrete pathways for security researchers, industry practitioners, and open-source developers to contribute technical feedback to ongoing policy rulemakings.

talks.title: The Coming War on Encryption Part 3
talks.teaser: EFF Director of Federal Affairs India McKinney analyzes legislative attempts to weaken end-to-end encryption in the US Congress, urging technical resistance.
talks.summary:
The Resurgence of the Encryption Wars

Despite decades of technical consensus establishing that cryptographic backdoors undermine global security, lawmakers frequently introduce legislation aimed at breaking end-to-end encryption.

Legislative Threats: EARN IT and the STOP CSAM Act

India McKinney analyzes dangerous bills advancing through the US Senate Judiciary Committee that impose severe liability on platforms offering end-to-end encrypted messaging.

The Regulatory and Law Enforcement Push for Client-Side Scanning

Federal law enforcement agencies continue lobbying for client-side scanning and mandatory access mandates that would fundamentally erode digital privacy.

Technological and Grassroots Advocacy

McKinney provides concrete strategies for engineers and civil society advocates to educate policymakers, defend cryptographic standards, and protect secure communications.

talks.title: Putting Your Money Where Your Cyber Is: Software Liability
talks.teaser: Law and engineering professor Andrea Matwyshyn analyzes Pillar 3 of the National Cybersecurity Strategy, exploring future legal frameworks for software liability.
talks.summary:
Shifting Liability to Software Manufacturers

Pillar 3 of the US National Cybersecurity Strategy proposes a paradigm shift in software law: rebalancing market incentives by holding commercial vendors liable for insecure software.

The Evolution of Security and Product Liability Law

Professor Andrea Matwyshyn traces the historical doctrine of software disclaimers, comparing software warranties to established product liability frameworks in physical goods.

Defining Standards of Care and Safe Harbors

Courts and regulators must establish objective criteria for 'reasonable security', defining safe harbor protections for vendors adhering to secure-by-design engineering practices.

Anticipating Legal and Economic Ramifications

The session engages attendees in structured legal exercises to debate edge cases, evaluate open-source exemptions, and inform forthcoming software liability legislation.

talks.title: Navigating the Digital Frontier: Advancing Cyber Diplomacy
talks.teaser: International diplomats and policy experts explore multilateral cyber negotiations at the United Nations and OAS, shaping global norms and confidence-building measures.
talks.summary:
The Global Landscape of Cyber Diplomacy

As geopolitical friction increasingly manifests in cyberspace, international diplomatic forums work to establish voluntary state norms and prevent unintended escalation.

Multilateral Dialogues at the United Nations and OAS

Panelists examine negotiations within the UN Open-Ended Working Group (OEWG), the Ad-Hoc Committee on Cybercrime, and the Organization of American States (OAS).

Building Cross-Border Trust and Capacity

Fostering confidence-building measures and providing cybersecurity capacity assistance to developing nations strengthens regional resilience and harmonizes cross-border cooperation.

The Role of Public-Private and Multistakeholder Partnerships

Effective cyber diplomacy requires continuous engagement with technical experts, academic institutions, and private industry to ground international law in technical reality.

talks.title: International Cyber Policy 101
talks.teaser: OECD and international government delegates outline global cyber policy priorities, consumer IoT security standards, and regulatory harmonization.
talks.summary:
Establishing Global Baselines in Cyber Policy

Governments worldwide are accelerating regulatory interventions in technology, creating a complex patchwork of compliance requirements across different jurisdictions.

Harmonizing Consumer IoT Security Standards

Peter Stephens of the OECD details the international adoption of baseline consumer IoT security frameworks (such as ETSI EN 303 645) across the UK, EU, Australia, and Singapore.

Priorities Across Allied Governments for 2023-24

Representatives from the UK and Australian governments and policy think tanks discuss emerging legislative agendas covering critical infrastructure, supply chains, and incident reporting.

Navigating the Global Regulatory Maze

The panel explores the challenges of international policy harmonization, discussing how multinational organizations can manage divergent regulatory mandates.

talks.title: How Hackers Can Work with Govt to Protect High-Risk Communities
talks.teaser: Explores scalable models for governments, civil society, and hackers to collaborate in defending high-risk communities and under-resourced civic organizations.
talks.summary:
The Vulnerability of High-Risk Civil Society Groups

Non-profit organizations, marginalized communities, and human rights defenders face persistent cyber threats while suffering from an acute global shortage of technical cybersecurity talent.

Overcoming the Cybersecurity Talent Gap

With hundreds of thousands of unfilled infosec positions, traditional market mechanisms fail to allocate necessary defensive resources to at-risk community groups.

Scaling Community Defense Collaborations

Panelists examine collaborative models where government initiatives, corporate volunteer programs, and hacker collectives partner to provide pro-bono security assistance.

Policy Solutions for Sustainable Cyber Resiliency

The session generates concrete policy recommendations for subsidizing security tooling, establishing regional defense clinics, and creating legal protections for volunteer responders.

talks.title: How Can We Encourage More Hackers to Engage with Policymakers?
talks.teaser: Examines 25 years of hacker-policymaker collaboration since L0pht's 1998 congressional testimony, drawing lessons for engaging with European technology regulators.
talks.summary:
A History of Hacker Policy Engagement

Since the seminal 1998 congressional testimony of the L0pht hacker collective, the US has developed unique channels for bringing technical hacker expertise directly into government policy.

Bridging the Gap Between European Regulators and Technologists

As the European Union crafts major technology regulations (such as the Cyber Resilience Act and AI Act), there is an urgent need to engage grassroots hackers in policy formulation.

Overcoming Cultural and Linguistic Barriers

Peter Stephens and Kranz analyze the cultural divide between bureaucratic policymaking circles and technical security researchers, identifying communication roadblocks.

Actionable Models for Researcher Advocacy

The speakers present practical roadmaps for technical researchers to participate in public consultations, legislative briefings, and advisory working groups.

talks.title: Demystifying Hacking for Government Officials
talks.teaser: The National Association of Secretaries of State (NASS) and security researchers share lessons from building trust and collaboration around election infrastructure.
talks.summary:
Building Bridges with State and Local Governments

State and local government officials oversee critical public services, including election administration and municipal utilities, but often lack technical familiarity with cybersecurity research.

The NASS Hacking Demystified Initiative

Panelists detail the 'Hacking Demystified' program created by the National Association of Secretaries of State (NASS), which connects election officials with ethical hackers in interactive workshops.

Overcoming Mutual Misconceptions and Fear

By engaging officials in live demonstrations, researchers help demystify vulnerability discovery, transforming adversarial perceptions into productive collaborative partnerships.

Expanding Collaborative Programs Nationwide

The session facilitates interactive brainstorming to scale researcher-government educational programs across state agencies and municipal bodies.

talks.title: Cyber Policy Adrift: Securing the Maritime Ecosystem
talks.teaser: Maritime cybersecurity experts examine the fragile global shipping ecosystem, outdated shipboard legacy systems, and the need for harmonized port policies.
talks.summary:
The Fragility of the Global Maritime Supply Chain

The global economy relies overwhelmingly on maritime shipping, yet ocean vessels and commercial seaports operate on legacy, under-funded, and poorly segregated OT networks.

Technical Realities of Shipboard and Port Infrastructure

Panelists explore the unique cybersecurity challenges of modern maritime systems, including satellite communication dependencies, Electronic Chart Display (ECDIS) flaws, and crane automation.

The Lack of Unified Governance and Enforcement

Navigating international waters involves fragmented jurisdictional boundaries, resulting in ambiguous regulatory oversight and weak enforcement of maritime cybersecurity standards.

Harmonizing International Maritime Cyber Policy

The discussion outlines proposals to harmonize US Coast Guard, International Maritime Organization (IMO), and European port security directives into a cohesive global framework.

talks.title: Blocking Pathways into Cybercrime: Current Efforts and Opportunities
talks.teaser: Law enforcement, defense attorneys, and former hackers discuss diversion programs redirecting young hackers away from cybercrime toward legitimate cybersecurity careers.
talks.summary:
The Shift Toward Cybercrime Prevention and Diversion

Traditional law enforcement responses to youth hacking have focused heavily on criminal prosecution, which often destroys potential careers and fails to deter underground cybercrime communities.

International Youth Diversion Programs

Panelists review groundbreaking prevention models developed in the UK (Cyber Prevent) and the Netherlands (Hack_Right), designed to identify at-risk youth and intervene before criminal conduct occurs.

Mentorship, Education, and Legal Pathways

Providing young technologists with ethical hacking mentors, educational workshops, and employment opportunities channels technical curiosity into productive defensive careers.

Perspectives from Former Hackers and Defense Counsel

A defense attorney and a former hacker share personal insights on navigating early legal pitfalls, emphasizing the transformative power of supportive community interventions.

talks.title: Beyond the Breach: Cyber Policy + Hacker Perspectives
talks.teaser: International policy hackers explore how hacker participation shapes global humanitarian cyber policies at the ICRC, OAS, and regional CSIRTs in Latin America.
talks.summary:
Integrating Hacker Perspectives into Multilateral Policy

Cyber policy formulation often occurs in diplomatic isolation, creating rules disconnected from technical realities unless security researchers actively participate in deliberations.

Humanitarian Norms and the ICRC Cyberspace Delegation

Panelists discuss initiatives within the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) to establish international humanitarian protections for civilian infrastructure and medical facilities during cyberwarfare.

Regional Collaboration Across the Americas and CSIRTs

Examining cybersecurity developments within the Organization of American States (OAS) and Latin American Computer Security Incident Response Teams (CSIRTs) highlights grassroots engagement models.

Creating Open Platforms for Policymaking Innovation

The panel outlines strategies for institutionalizing hacker representation in regional digital forensics, cyber diplomacy, and international threat response frameworks.

talks.title: All Your Vulns Are Belong to Terms and Conditions
talks.teaser: Deconstructs global Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure (CVD) policies, government equities processes, and regulatory mandates like the EU Cyber Resilience Act.
talks.summary:
The Complexities of Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure

While Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure (CVD) is widely celebrated in security theory, executing disclosures across diverse corporate sectors remains fraught with delays, misunderstandings, and legal friction.

Navigating the Regulatory Alphabet Soup: CRA, NIS2, and VDPs

The speaker demystifies emerging international regulatory mandates—including the European Union's Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) and NIS2 directive—that impose statutory disclosure timelines.

Understanding Government Vulnerabilities Equities Processes (VEP)

An in-depth explanation unpacks how national governments evaluate zero-day vulnerabilities, balancing defensive patch coordination against intelligence and offensive retention equities.

Bridging the Divide Between Policymakers and Researchers

The presentation calls for standardized disclosure lexicons and practical CVD legal frameworks to protect ethical researchers while holding recalcitrant vendors accountable.

talks.title: A Global Approach to Tackling Software Resilience
talks.teaser: International government representatives explore global strategies for software supply chain resilience, government procurement standards, and regulatory incentives.
talks.summary:
The Systemic Imperative of Software Supply Chain Resilience

As software permeates every facet of critical infrastructure and modern commerce, systemic vulnerabilities and software supply chain attacks represent global economic risks.

International Government Approaches to Software Security

Representatives from allied governments discuss strategies to improve baseline software resilience, ranging from mandatory security standards to leveraging public procurement purchasing power.

Engaging the Developer and Hacker Communities

Effective regulation requires direct collaboration with open-source maintainers, software engineers, and vulnerability researchers to align security mandates with actual development workflows.

Building Harmonized Global Standards

The panel explores international coordination mechanisms to establish cohesive, mutually recognized software resilience benchmarks across global supply chains.
